text: The Möbius function μ(n) (莫比乌斯函数): μ(1) = 1; μ(n) = (−1)k if n is a product of k distinct primes; μ(n) = 0 if a square divides n. Its key property: Σd | n μ(d) = [n = 1], i.e. 1 when n = 1 and 0 otherwise. It comes out of the linear sieve (进阶篇第19章).

That property turns a condition into a sum: [gcd(i, j) = 1] = Σd | gcd(i, j) μ(d). Swap the order of summation (sum over d first) and the condition disappears. This is Möbius inversion (莫比乌斯反演) as it is used in contests.

Step Count pairs i ≤ a, j ≤ b with gcd(i, j) = 1 condition as a sum Σi Σj Σd | i, d | j μ(d) sum over d first Σd μ(d) · (number of multiples of d up to a) · (… up to b) closed form Σd=1..min(a,b) μ(d) · ⌊a/d⌋ · ⌊b/d⌋ fast division blocks (进阶篇第19章) + prefix sums of μ: O(√a + √b) per query
ZAP-Queries (P3455): pairs with gcd exactly d become coprime pairs after dividing by d. The block ends where either quotient changes: r = min(a/(a/l), b/(b/l)).
a = 4, b = 5, d = 2: pairs (2, 2), (2, 4), (4, 2): 3. With a lower bound too (Problem b, P2522), use inclusion- exclusion over four such counts.

title: 欧拉函数与 gcd 求和

text: gcd as Σ φ(d); the general recipe.

Sums of gcds use φ instead: n = Σd | n φ(d), so gcd(i, j) = Σd | i, d | j φ(d). Summing over d first: Σi,j ≤ n gcd(i, j) = Σd φ(d) ⌊n/d⌋² (P2398). Same pattern: write the value as a divisor sum, swap the sums, use blocks.

General recipe: (1) replace the gcd condition or value by a divisor sum (μ for "= 1", φ for "the gcd itself"); (2) bring the divisor sum outside; (3) count multiples with ⌊n/d⌋; (4) prefix sums + division blocks. YY 的 GCD (P2257) sums over prime gcds with precomputed Σ μ(k/p).
n = 2: gcds 1, 1, 1, 2 sum to 5. The tests for 10 and 100 are checked against a direct double loop in Python.
Products of numbers like ⌊n/d⌋² reach 10¹⁰ for n = 10⁵: keep everything in long long.
Make the sieve range cover the largest a / d (or n) of every query, and compute the prefix sums once, outside the query loop: recomputing per query makes the "fast" method O(n) per query again.
